description: One exact hologram holds many items at once, and one pass applies a weighted sum of operators to all of them. A Pleroma stores items (a key, and optionally a flag word, an arrangement and a tick) as exact counts in one fixed array, reads exact counts by key, whole item, flag word, arrangement and tick (joint counts over faces are opt-in), and refuses past its key capacity rather than answering wrongly. Relabelling, ageing, diffusion, key shifts and binding two stores act on every stored item in one pass, and flag flips, arrangement relabellings and time shifts summed into a PleromaKernel apply in one pass. The same store backs an aggregate plane for database queries and a page store with parity repair and restore points; CycleHologram adds exact multiset reconciliation between replicas. PleromaArrangementBand holds arrangements of any number of things (ranked ballots) and answers every question on up to a chosen number of places exactly, with a check built into its cells. PleromaFlagBand holds words of up to 64 flags (survey answers, feature flags) and answers every question on up to a chosen number of flags exactly. Every store carries two upper bounds, Mass and Peak, that each operation moves by its own rule, so ReadsCertified and InnerProductCertified prove a read or a join count exact without a pass over the data. KeyedSummary holds an exact 64-bit count and a 128-bit sum per measure for each dense key, with all-or-nothing batches, a one-pass fold through a key-to-group map, exact top-k, pre-grouped group totals that stay exact as facts arrive and as keys change groups, and checksummed persistence; Crc32C is the CRC-32C checksum it uses, hardware-accelerated where the CPU has the instruction. Beneath it all is the phasor Vector Symbolic Architecture (VSA) codec: bind, unbind, bundle and correlate over unit-complex faces, with a frozen-identity codec for models and a width-configurable SIMD codec for storage and similarity search. No dependencies beyond System and System.Numerics.
title: Phasor
